crossRefs.note: All the king’s servants who were in the king’s gate bowed down, and paid homage to Haman; for the king had so commanded…
Then Haman went out that day joyful and glad of heart, but when Haman saw Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he didn’t…
But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by the eunuchs. Therefore the king was very angry, and…
but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.
Yahweh said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?
For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.
A fool shows his annoyance the same day, but one who overlooks an insult is prudent.
A hot-tempered man must pay the penalty, for if you rescue him, you must do it again.
The proud and arrogant man—“Scoffer” is his name— he works in the arrogance of pride.
A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden; but a fool’s provocation is heavier than both.
Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; but who is able to stand before jealousy?
Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and…

people.name: Haman
people.line: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.

people.name: Mordecai
people.line: Esther's cousin, a Jewish leader in the Persian court.

translations.web: When Haman saw that Mordecai didn’t bow down, nor pay him homage, Haman was full of wrath.
translations.bsb: When Haman saw that Mordecai would not bow down or pay him homage, he was filled with rage.
translations.kjv: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.
translations.asv: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not down, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.
